results.title: DeepSeek V4.1-Flash: KV-Cache schrumpft deutlich – warum Samsung & SK Hynix dennoch reagieren
results.content: Der Kernpunkt, der die Kursbewegung ausgelöst haben dürfte, ist die KV-Cache-Reduktion – allerdings in einem engeren Sinn als die Schlagzeilen vermuten lassen. DeepSeek beschreibt in seinem technischen Report auf Hugging Face, dass CSA2, FP4 Key-Value Caching und SWA Bounded Replay den globalen KV-Cache-Footprint auf rund 890 Byte pro Token senken, also auf etwa ein Viertel im Vergleich zu DeepSeek-V4-Flash. Zusätzlich nennt das Unternehmen, dass persistentes KV-Storage auf ungefähr ein Achtel [...] genannt, danach für das zweite Quartal weitere 58 % bis 63 %. Bei NAND Flash beziffert TrendForce das Wachstum der Kontraktpreise im zweiten Quartal auf 70 % bis 75 %. Wenn Investoren solche Bewegungen bereits im Blick haben, reicht eine technisch klingende Effizienzstory oft aus, um kurzfristig die Annahmen zur Nachfragekurve zu hinterfragen. [...] – DeepSeek hat mit V4.1-Flash ein neues Modell vorgestellt, das laut Hersteller den KV-Cache deutlich reduziert. Die Recheneffizienz kommt beim Markt so schnell an, dass Samsung und SK Hynix am 11. September spürbar nachgaben. Gleichzeitig ist die technische Kernaussage enger als die Börsenreaktion: Es geht primär um temporären Inferenz-Speicher, nicht um den kompletten Hardware-Mix. Für Anbieter und Käufer von KI-Infrastruktur verschiebt die Meldung damit vor allem die Diskussion über Kosten

results.title: SK hynix Developing New NAND Products for KV Cache ...
results.content: KV cache is temporary data required for graphics processing units (GPUs) to handle AI computations. As AI data surges, the high-bandwidth memory (HBM) capacity for storing KV cache is reaching its limits. In response, SK hynix plans to develop new products that mount high-capacity NAND products near the GPU, allowing them to serve as an additional KV cache repository. DeepSeek's New AI Model Spooked Samsung and SK Hynix Investors

DeepSeek says V4.1-Flash cuts its KV cache memory use to a quarter of the prior model. Samsung and SK Hynix investors treated that narrow technical claim like a warning shot at the whole AI memory trade. [...] Here's the catch. The memory claim is narrower than the share-price reaction made it look. DeepSeek's Hugging Face technical report says CSA2, FP4 key-value caching and SWA Bounded Replay reduce the global KV cache footprint to roughly 890 bytes per token, about one quarter of DeepSeek-V4-Flash. It also says persistent KV storage falls to about one eighth of the prior model. A Yahoo Finance article carried through Stocktwits framed the same point as a pressure point for Samsung and SK Hynix, [...] Home › Ai

# DeepSeek's New AI Model Spooked Samsung and SK Hynix Investors

DeepSeek's new V4.1 Flash model claims a fourfold cut in KV cache memory use, and Korean investors reacted fast: Samsung fell 3.5% and SK Hynix 2.2% in Seoul on September 11 while Micron and SanDisk held steady in the US. The drop came just two days after Goldman Sachs called a bottom in the memory downturn, complicating the idea that DeepSeek alone drove the selloff.

Ron Patel

results.title: Decoding the Jargon and Impact on Samsung, SK Hynix
results.content:
The problem emerged as AI began processing data equivalent to dozens of books at once. The notepad (KV cache) fills up almost instantly, creating a bottleneck. Previously, the only option was to spend enormous sums simply adding more memory chips. [...] The anxiety deepened when Matthew Prince, CEO of Cloudflare, hailed TurboQuant as "Google's DeepSeek moment." Yet the view from the industry and securities analysts is entirely different. They say the market's panic is simply a misunderstanding born of unfamiliar technical jargon, and that the real signal is a virtuous cycle that will dramatically expand the AI semiconductor market.

Tokens Are AI's Dictionary, KV Cache Is Its Notepad, TurboQuant Is Tiny Handwriting [...] To understand what TurboQuant is and what impact it may have, one must first decode the alien terminology. AI reads human language by breaking it into units called tokens — fragments of words. As a conversation grows longer, the AI temporarily writes down earlier tokens' context in memory such as HBM so it does not lose track. It is like sticking Post-it notes beside a thick book to remember the content. This temporary AI notepad is called the KV cache (Key-Value Cache).
